gloss: way of calling, how to address

definitions.gloss: way of calling, how to address, what to call something
definitions.explanation: The manner or term used to address or refer to a person or thing. Often used when discussing what name, title, or term is appropriate for someone or something.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}の{呼|よ}び{方|かた}がわからない。
examples.english: I don't know how to address the teacher.

examples.japanese: {日本|にほん}では{名字|みょうじ}で{呼|よ}ぶのが{普通|ふつう}の{呼|よ}び{方|かた}です。
examples.english: In Japan, calling people by their surname is the normal way of addressing them.

examples.japanese: この{魚|さかな}は{地域|ちいき}によって{呼|よ}び{方|かた}が{違|ちが}うので、{旅行先|りょこうさき}で{戸惑|とまど}うことがある。
examples.english: This fish has different names depending on the region, which can be confusing when traveling.

notes:
USAGE:
{呼|よ}び{方|かた} is formed from {呼|よ}ぶ (to call) + {方|かた} (way of doing). It is a very common word in everyday conversation, especially when discussing appropriate forms of address or regional naming differences.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {呼|よ}び{方|かた}がわからない: not know what to call (someone/something)
- {呼|よ}び{方|かた}が{違|ちが}う: have different names for
- {正|ただ}しい{呼|よ}び{方|かた}: correct way to address
- {呼|よ}び{方|かた}を{変|か}える: to change how one addresses (someone)
